newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to lift 2-tier baht at appropriate time.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to lift 2-tier baht at appropriate time.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Tuesday Thailand's two-tier baht system would be lifted only at an appropriate time when its monetary sector gains stability.
Chaiyawat said: "We will scrap the two-tier system only at an appropriate time and when conditions in the money market are stable."

Assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee said earlier on Tuesday the bank was reviewing the system adopted since mid-May to block supply of offshore baht for speculators who had attacked the baht.
Both Chaiyawat and Siri did not indicate whether and when the central bank would actually scrap the two-tier system.
Chaiyawat said any changes in Thailand's foreign exchange controls would be taken based on its national interests. He did not elaborate.
Thailand imposed the two-tier system in mid-May to cut off access of offshore baht supply to speculators who had shorted the baht in their earlier attacks on the currency.
Dealers said the two-tier system has been made less essential for boosting baht stability after Thailand announced a de facto devaluation of the currency on July 2.
The baht has since depreciated almost 25 percent.
Dealers said as part of Thailand's decision to enter the IMF financial assistance programme, it may have to agree to ease its foreign exchange controls.
